findings.detail: The spec states that Security N/A is an explicit adverse result that can never produce CONTINUE. It also states that the single retry cannot be used to shop for a better verdict. The normative scan does not support either statement. walk() flags only verdict:FAIL, severity:CRITICAL, and four hard categories, and the matched_signals enum is limited to those values. An invalid attempt 1 can carry any of the following and still scan NONE: gates.security.verdict 'N/A', routing 'HARD_STOP' or 'ESCALATE_FOUNDER', or requires_human true. Such a response receives RETRY_IDENTICAL, and attempt 2 can replace it with PASS/CONTINUE. The result is a fail-open path around the Security N/A hard stop. Required fix: add adverse signals for verdict:N/A on the security gate, routing:HARD_STOP, routing:ESCALATE_FOUNDER, and requires_human:true. Update the schema enum, the spec text, and the scanner, and add vectors for each signal.
findings.title: Adverse-signal scan omits Security N/A and adverse routing values, so an invalid hard-stop response can be retried into a better verdict

findings.detail: The routing table and routing() check RESERVED_ACT_REQUIRED before the Security FAIL/N-A rule. As a result, Security N/A plus any RESERVED_ACT_REQUIRED finding derives ESCALATE_FOUNDER. The final allOf clause of review-result.schema.json, however, unconditionally requires routing const HARD_STOP whenever Security is N/A. A correctly derived result in this case is therefore schema-invalid, and the contract cannot represent its own routing table. That case falls into controller-side invalidity and action_required, and the ESCALATE_FOUNDER route is lost. No vector covers this combination. Required fix: make the schema clause conditional on the absence of RESERVED_ACT_REQUIRED findings, or drop the clause and rely on the controller derivation. Then add a schema vector for Security N/A combined with a reserved-act finding.
findings.title: Result schema forces HARD_STOP whenever Security is N/A, contradicting routing rule 1 (RESERVED_ACT_REQUIRED → ESCALATE_FOUNDER)

findings.detail: Spec §6 describes the missing-ratification outcome as a hard stop. Amendment 0001 defines it as the controller-side outcome ESCALATE_FOUNDER and says explicitly that it is not called HARD_STOP. Align the spec wording with the amendment so that the controller-outcome taxonomy is unambiguous.
findings.title: Spec says the controller must 'hard-stop with ESCALATE_FOUNDER' while the amendment says this outcome is not called HARD_STOP
